newsitem.title: PARAGUAY: Paraguay seeks Stroessner son's secret millions.
newsitem.headline: Paraguay seeks Stroessner son's secret millions.

text.p: Paraguayan congressmen said on Tuesday they want to recover from European and U.S. banks an estimated $300 million plundered from the state by the son of former dictator Alfredo Stroessner.

Legislators have set up a committee to investigate bank accounts in Geneva, New York and Miami in the name of Gustavo Stroessner, son of the general who ruled this central South American republic with an iron hand for nearly 35 years.

"We believe that if we act quickly it could be possible to recover at least part of the immense fortune these people built up by defrauding the Paraguayan people," opposition Sen. Basilio Nikkiphoroff told reporters.

Gen. Stroessner and his son have lived in exile in Brazil since the 1989 coup that paved the way for democracy. Brazil has rejected demands for their extradition to Paraguay to face trial for alleged crimes committed during the dictatorship.

The secret of Gustavo Stroessner's foreign bank accounts was revealed by his ex-wife, Maria Eugenia Heikel. Paraguayan Prosecutor-General Anibal Cabrera quickly began moves to put restrictions on the Stroessner bank accounts abroad.
"Historic and political conditions are now right to guarantee a fair but implacable trial against those who committed crimes against the Paraguayan state," said Cabrera.
In 1974, when the general was still in power, Readers' Digest magazine listed the general as one of the 10 richest men in the world, estimating his fortune at over $1 billion.
Paraguay, a landlocked country of 5 million, has an annual per capita income of $1,340 and official data says 84 percent of the rural population lives in extreme poverty.
